title: Hampton hands him an electric bass or two weeks and fare home
summary: On the first night Hampton gave Monk a Fender bass; angry and embarrassed, he chose to learn it since he could not go home.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: How did you cope with playing with that band?

Well, what happened, the very first thing happened, right there that night, Hamp walked up and handed me an electric bass. Just handed it to me. He'd gotten it from the company. Said, 'Gates, this is the sound I want on the band, so...' So I said, 'Hey, man, you called...when I called you,

you told me to bring my bass. You told me you wanted me to play the bass. I don't know nothing about electric bass. I never... This is the second one I've ever saw. I came here to play my bass; you hired me for it.'
So he said, well, there'd be no hard feelings if I didn't want to play it, he understood. He said, 'Then I'll just give you two weeks salary and your fare back home.' No way.

I just left home, right? I didn't come for that. In fact, they had a big farewell party for me before I left. You know, 'I'm going out to California with Hamp.' I couldn't go back home; I couldn't think of going back home. I just left home.

I took it. And when I took it, I was very angry inside. I don't know when I've been that bitter inside. I really was an angry man inside, because I really loved my music, my bass and what I was doing and I'd thought that's what he wanted. You know, I thought that's what I was coming out there for. So embarrassed. I was so embarrassed I didn't know what to do.
But he didn't expect you to play it the first night. You couldn't.

No. Well, the guy...Hampton...to know him...I'm indebted to Hamp for all those years, not just because of that but...When I took it, I remember, I came back to where we were staying, the cottage, and I knew I had to have that job. I knew I had to stay with Hamp. That's what I came for. I knew that.

I had also a real job on my hands, maybe a problem, to be able to play that instrument. Because he had made it very clear that's what... (Inaudible) . Now I'm thinking, I've got to make the choice. It's gotta be, it can't be half way. Because once again, here I am. I can't halfway.

I knew I had to make a decision to play the instrument if I took it, or go home. And I, like, it outweighed it, because I couldn't go home. But I knew if I was gonna take the instrument and play it, I was gonna play it well, the best I could. There was no time for jiving around. I was gonna play it. (end of Master Cassette I/cassette copy II)
